record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: For the numerical fixed-point construction of static or stationary Vlasov steady states, can one prove that the iteration map has a fixed point? In the simplified Vlasov-Poisson setting, the map takes an input spatial density ρ, computes its gravitational potential Uρ, substitutes Uρ into a prescribed particle ansatz Φ(E,L), renormalizes the resulting density to the prescribed total mass M by an amplitude K, and returns T(ρ)=K(ρ̃)ρ̃. The same fixed-point question should be settled for the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system and for the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system.

evidence.quote: We now define an amplitude K(˜ρ) = M (∫ ˜ρ(x) dx)−1 so that the new spatial density K(˜ρ) ˜ρ again has mass M. Let us consider the map T : D → D defined by T (ρ) = K(˜ρ)˜ρ.

It is an open problem to show that the map T has a fixed point. Similar fixed point problems, based on the same strategy, can be formulated for several related systems; e.g. the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system and the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system. It is an open problem in each case to show the existence of a fixed point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a self-gravitating collisionless ensemble of identical particles described by a phase-space distribution function f(x,v) on R^3 × R^3. In the (Newtonian) Vlasov–Poisson setting one looks for time-independent solutions of the system

    v·∂_x f − ∂_x U·∂_v f = 0,    ΔU = 4π ρ,    ρ(x) = ∫_{R^3} f(x,v) dv,

with U(x) → 0 as |x| → ∞. Fix a prescribed total mass M > 0, and a prescribed "particle ansatz" Φ : R × [0,∞) → [0,∞) that is to be evaluated on the particle energy E = (1/2)|v|^2 + U(x) and the modulus of angular momentum L = |x×v|. Let D be the set of admissible nonnegative, integrable spatial densities ρ on R^3 with ∫ρ = M and suitable decay.

Define the iteration map T : D → D as follows. Given ρ ∈ D:
(i) solve ΔU_ρ = 4π ρ with U_ρ(x) → 0 at infinity, obtaining the induced gravitational potential U_ρ;
(ii) form the candidate density

    ρ̃(x) := ∫_{R^3} Φ( (1/2)|v|^2 + U_ρ(x), |x×v| ) dv;

(iii) define the amplitude K(ρ̃) := M ( ∫_{R^3} ρ̃(y) dy )^{−1}, and set

    T(ρ) := K(ρ̃) ρ̃.

Problem. Prove that, for a suitable class of ansatz functions Φ and an appropriately chosen domain D, the map T admits a fixed point ρ_* ∈ D (which then yields a stationary solution of the corresponding Vlasov-type system with total mass M).

Pose and solve the analogous fixed-point existence problem for:
(a) the Newtonian Vlasov–Poisson system, as described above;
(b) the spherically symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system, in which U_ρ is replaced by the metric functions determined from ρ (and its associated momentum/pressure components) via the spherically symmetric Einstein equations, and Φ depends on the corresponding relativistic conserved quantities (particle energy and angular momentum);
(c) the axially symmetric stationary Einstein–Vlasov system, in which the metric is determined from the matter via the axisymmetric stationary Einstein equations and Φ depends on the corresponding conserved quantities (energy and the axial angular momentum).

In each case, establish existence of a fixed point of the corresponding map T.
artifact.status_search_result: The spherically symmetric Vlasov–Poisson case (a) has been settled: a 2024 preprint proves existence of a fixed point for the mass-preserving iteration map T producing spherically symmetric steady states of the Vlasov–Poisson system. The analogous fixed-point existence problems for the spherically symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system and for the axially symmetric (stationary) Einstein–Vlasov system appear to remain open; a generalization to flat axially symmetric solutions is mentioned as a desired next step.

status_evidence.title: Steady states of the spherically symmetric Vlasov-Poisson system as fixed points of a mass-preserving algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that under suitable assumptions a fixed point to this problem exists in the case of the spherically symmetric Vlasov-Poisson system.
status_evidence.claim: The Vlasov-Poisson spherically symmetric fixed-point case is solved.

status_evidence.title: Steady states of the spherically symmetric Vlasov-Poisson system as fixed points of a mass-preserving algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: A generalization of this result to the case of flat axially symmetric solutions would prove that steady states obtained numerically exist.
status_evidence.claim: The axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov fixed-point problem is still posed as a goal, indicating it remains open.
